author: reek
body: Until now a scope literal was a compile-time lint and nothing more: the checker refused an out-of-scope path it could SEE (CDX4002, keyed on the operation's name), and any path the program computed instead of spelling walked straight past the promise. The grant was binding on literals and on nothing else. Here the scope reaches the disk: the boot grant writes it into proc 0's process-table entry, and Fat16 asks for it before it touches a sector.

author: reek
body: The paths here are literals only because they are easier to read. The fat16-* functions are ordinary functions and not effect operations, so the compile-time check does not key on them at all -- nothing rejected this program at compile time, and the refusals below are the running machine's.
